evals.name: angular-saved-filters
evals.prompt: I want to add saved filters to the recipe search in our Angular app — you pick a few filters, name the combo, and it shows up as a chip you can click later. Before I start building it let's write a design doc.
evals.expected_output: design-docs/<slug>.md containing all six chapters in order, each written after its own round of interview questions, with a hand-back menu between chapters. An interview log showing concrete, proposal-shaped options.

assertions.name: doc-written-to-design-docs
assertions.text: A single design doc markdown file exists under design-docs/.

assertions.name: six-chapters-exact-order
assertions.text: The doc contains exactly the six required H2 chapters — Goals, Non-Goals, Desired Behavior, Design & Implementation Details, Testing Strategy, Alternatives Considered — in that order, with no extra or missing chapters.

assertions.name: no-chapter-left-pending
assertions.text: No chapter is left as _Pending._ or empty at the end of the run.

assertions.name: interviewed-chapter-by-chapter
assertions.text: The interview log contains at least 6 distinct question rounds, and they appear in chapter order rather than as one upfront question dump before any writing.

assertions.name: handback-menu-between-chapters
assertions.text: At least 5 next-step / hand-back menus appear in the log, each offering a continue option plus a revise or dig-deeper option.

assertions.name: options-are-concrete-proposals
assertions.text: At least 70% of the logged options are concrete, specific proposals the user could paste into the doc — not abstract categories like Simple/Complex, Yes/No, or Option A/Option B.

assertions.name: multiselect-and-preview-used
assertions.text: The log contains at least one question with multiSelect: true and at least one option carrying a preview.

assertions.name: non-goals-carry-reasons
assertions.text: Every entry in the Non-Goals chapter states why not, or not yet — no bare list items.

assertions.name: alternatives-name-revisit-trigger
assertions.text: Alternatives Considered says why each alternative lost, and at least one entry names a concrete condition that would make the team revisit it.

assertions.name: goals-are-outcome-shaped
assertions.text: The Goals chapter states outcomes, not solutions — no specific implementation (localStorage, a library, a component name) is named as a goal.

assertions.name: persona-constraints-recorded
assertions.text: The doc records Sam's actual stated constraints: localStorage for v1 with server sync deferred, no new state management library, testing through the component with faked HTTP rather than isolated store unit tests, and the stale-diet-tag edge case.

evals.name: redis-session-migration
evals.prompt: we're moving session storage off the in-memory map onto redis because we're about to run more than one node. can you put a design doc in design-docs for it
evals.expected_output: Same six-chapter doc, in a backend/infra domain. Testing Strategy should address the seam (what talks to a real Redis vs. what is faked) and Alternatives Considered should carry revisit triggers.

evals.name: resume-partial-doc
evals.prompt: let's continue the design doc for offline mode
evals.expected_output: Resumes at Desired Behavior. The existing Goals and Non-Goals chapters are left byte-identical, not rewritten or re-interviewed.

assertions.name: existing-chapters-untouched
assertions.text: The pre-existing Goals and Non-Goals chapters are byte-identical to the fixture — not rewritten, reworded, or reordered.

assertions.name: resumed-at-desired-behavior
assertions.text: The run resumed at Desired Behavior: the log contains no interview questions re-litigating Goals or Non-Goals, and the first question round is about Desired Behavior.

assertions.name: no-chapter-left-pending
assertions.text: The four remaining chapters are filled in; no _Pending._ placeholder is left.
